data.outcome_summary: This OECD report uses PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment data to examine how 15-year-old students generate and express creative ideas across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. It explains that the original PISA scoring awarded full/partial/no credit using coding procedures designed for cross-cultural comparability, but that this approach cannot identify the most creative responses within each participating country/economy. To address this, the report describes a rescoring project in which two more granular scoring methods—Holistic Judgement (1–7) and Criteria-Based scoring (appropriateness, originality, value, and flexibility where applicable)—were applied to a random sample of genuine student responses. The report then uses the rescored data to illustrate patterns in creative responses, including examples from disadvantaged students (lowest ESCS decile) and qualitative themes across tasks. The excerpt does not provide model-based performance metrics or specify PV/missing-data handling, so quantitative effect sizes and statistical uncertainty cannot be verified from the provided text.
